main_text.l: testimonio in animis ipsorum ab ista iniquita-
te in suos fratres revocari. Natura enim omnes
ignorantes rerum spiritualium esse, donec eas
nos Deus docuerit: nec plus cognitionis de
illis posse nobis contingere, quàm prout de suo
lumine Deus accenderit demensum fidei. Ex-
perientia vero vitæ ante-actæ nostræ id ipsum
testari luculentissimè cùm omnes à naturâ
infideles se fuisse sibi sint conscij, &c abreptos
fuisse post idola muta & mundi vanitate prout
contigerit: neque tum fuisse futurum gratum
iustumq. nobis officiu, dum illis tenebris cir-
cumclusi hærebamus, si quisinsolète[?] fastu nos
in tenebris siuisset computrescere. Postremò
autem præsentem gratiæ diuinæ infirmos susti-
nentis &c cæcos illustrantis conscientiam satis
ostendere tenues illas scintillas diuinæ lucis non
exsufflandas fastu, aut contemptu extinguen-
das esse; sed magni semper faciendas, velut spi-
ritus Dei munera; quæ ne in minimis quidem
puerulis oporteat contristari. Et quis dubitat,
quin in eo ipso dicentium numero, quos hic
commendat Dauid, fuerint homines omnis
generis secundũ dona Spiritus & gradus scien-
tiæ, qui temporibus illis poterant contingere,
inter se distinguendi? fuerunt docti; indocti,
firmi, infirmi, excelsi, mediocres, tenues, om-
nes in eodem sermone pro modulo donationis
Christi occupati: de quibus omnibus prorsifcuè[?]
Dauid lætatus est, ad Christum commune

page.notes: The text begins mid-sentence and is a continuation from the previous page. The printed text runs on without indents, so it is set as one paragraph. Hyphenated words at line ends are kept with their printed hyphens: "iniquita-", "ante-actæ", "cir-", "susti-", "extinguen-", "spi-", "scien-", "om-", "prorsif-". Doubtful readings: "quisinsolète" (line 13), "prorsifcuè" (lines 29–30), and the running head "EIRENICI", which is printed with spaced letters. The bottom of the scan is cut off at the last line, and "commune" continues onto the next page. "secundũ" is printed with a tilde over the u, as shown in the scan.
